provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Review of Second Term
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall entrepreneurship concepts in cosmetology, explain customer care principles, list beauty business types, and identify key business terms.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about entrepreneurship and customer care in the beauty industry. Today we will refresh our memory on these important topics.
Content:
Entrepreneurship in cosmetology involves starting and managing a beauty business. Customer care is how we treat clients to make them happy and return. Business types include salon, spa, and mobile services. Terms like capital, profit, and loss are important to understand. For example, starting a salon with 50,000 naira capital requires planning for rent, equipment, and products.
Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to create a simple business plan for a small salon, listing possible expenses and expected income.
Evaluation questions:
What is entrepreneurship? Name two types of beauty businesses. What does customer care involve? How is capital different from profit? What is one challenge of starting a beauty business?
Summary:
Reviewing these concepts helps build a strong foundation for our beauty business studies this term.

topics.title: Product Knowledge
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify common cosmetics, explain safety precautions when using products, differentiate between skin types, and demonstrate proper product storage.
Introduction:
We use many cosmetics in our daily lives and in salons. Today we will learn how to identify them and use them safely.
Content:
Cosmetics are products used to enhance beauty. They include makeup, skincare, and hair products. Safety precautions include patch testing for allergies, checking expiry dates, and following instructions. Skin types are normal, oily, dry, and combination. For example, a danfo driver might need oil-control products while someone in harmattan season needs moisturizers. Products should be stored in cool, dry places away from sunlight.
Class activity:
Students will bring samples of different cosmetics and identify their uses, then practice proper storage techniques.
Evaluation questions:
Name three types of cosmetics. Why should we check product expiry dates? What are the four skin types? How should cosmetics be stored? What is patch testing?
Summary:
Knowing your products and using them safely is essential for any beauty professional.

topics.title: Branding and Packaging
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain what branding is, identify key elements of brand identity, design a simple logo, and discuss packaging importance.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about products. Today we will learn how to create a brand identity for beauty products.
Content:
Branding is creating a unique name, design, and image for a product. Brand identity includes logo, colors, and packaging. A good brand makes products stand out in the market like popular Nigerian beauty brands. Packaging protects the product and attracts customers. For example, shea butter packaged in colorful containers with African designs sells better than plain packaging. Your brand should reflect your values and target customers.
Class activity:
Students will design a logo and packaging for a new beauty product like a local hair oil or soap.
Evaluation questions:
What is branding? Name three elements of brand identity. Why is packaging important? How does branding help a business? What should you consider when designing packaging?
Summary:
Strong branding and attractive packaging can make your beauty products more successful in the market.

topics.title: Marketing Strategies
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain social media marketing, identify two referral methods, create a simple marketing post, and discuss customer retention.
Introduction:
Having good products and branding is not enough. Customers need to know about your business through marketing strategies.
Content:
Social media marketing uses platforms like Instagram and Facebook to promote beauty services. Customer referrals happen when satisfied customers tell others about your salon. For example, a market woman might tell her friends about a good hair stylist she found. Marketing posts should show before-and-after results, special offers, and new services. Retaining customers is cheaper than finding new ones through loyalty programs and excellent service.
Class activity:
Students will create a social media post promoting a beauty service and practice giving a referral script to a satisfied customer.
Evaluation questions:
What is social media marketing? How do customer referrals work? Why is customer retention important? What should be included in a marketing post? Name two social media platforms useful for beauty businesses.
Summary:
Effective marketing strategies help beauty businesses attract and keep more customers.

topics.title: Midterm Examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate knowledge of first term concepts through written examination.
Introduction:
Today we will have our midterm examination to assess your understanding of the topics covered so far this term.
Content:
The examination will cover entrepreneurship, product knowledge, branding and packaging, and marketing strategies. Questions will include definitions, short answers, and practical applications. You will have 45 minutes to complete the exam. Remember to read each question carefully before answering. Your work should be neat and organized.
Class activity:
Students will individually complete the midterm examination paper.
Evaluation questions:
The midterm examination will serve as the evaluation for this week.
Summary:
The midterm examination helps both you and I understand your progress in the beauty and cosmetology course so far.

topics.title: Setting Up a Beauty Business
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list steps to start a beauty business, calculate basic startup costs, design a simple salon layout, and identify essential equipment.
Introduction:
Last week we had our midterm exam. Today we will learn how to set up a beauty business from scratch.
Content:
Steps to start a beauty business include market research, business planning, and securing capital. Startup costs include rent, equipment, products, and licenses. A salon layout should have reception, washing area, treatment rooms, and storage. Essential equipment includes chairs, mirrors, trolleys, and sterilizers. For example, starting a small salon might cost 200,000 naira for rent, furniture, and initial products. The layout should be practical for both workers and clients.
Class activity:
Students will draw a simple layout for a small beauty salon on graph paper, labeling different areas and equipment needed.
Evaluation questions:
What are the first three steps to start a beauty business? Name four startup costs. What areas should be in a salon layout? Why is proper equipment important? How much capital might be needed for a small salon?
Summary:
Careful planning when setting up a beauty business increases the chances of success.

topics.title: Midterm Break
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to relax and recharge for the second half of the term.
Introduction:
This is our midterm break time. Use this period to rest and prepare for the remaining topics.
Content:
During this break, you should rest and spend time with family. You may also use this time to research beauty careers or practice skills learned so far. Remember to stay safe and return refreshed for our next classes. The break will help you come back with renewed energy for your studies.
Class activity:
No formal class activity during break period.
Evaluation questions:
No formal evaluation during break period.
Summary:
Enjoy your break and return ready to continue your beauty and cosmetology journey.

topics.title: Health and Safety in the Salon F
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain first aid procedures, demonstrate hygiene practices, identify salon hazards, and discuss sterilization methods.
Introduction:
Working in a salon requires attention to health and safety to protect both clients and workers.
Content:
First aid procedures include treating minor cuts, burns, and allergic reactions. Hygiene practices involve washing hands, wearing gloves, and cleaning tools regularly. Salon hazards include slippery floors, chemical exposure, and electrical faults. Sterilization methods include boiling, using alcohol, and autoclaving tools. For example, if a client gets a small cut while styling hair, you should clean it with antiseptic and apply a bandage immediately. All equipment should be cleaned after each client.
Class activity:
Students will practice proper handwashing technique and demonstrate how to sterilize hair tools using different methods.
Evaluation questions:
What are three first aid procedures for salon injuries? Why is hygiene important in salons? Name two salon hazards. How should tools be sterilized? What would you do if a client had an allergic reaction to a product?
Summary:
Maintaining health and safety standards is crucial for any successful beauty salon.

topics.title: Beauty Career Opportunities
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list five beauty careers, explain educational requirements for each, discuss career progression paths, and identify needed skills.
Introduction:
There are many career paths available in the beauty industry beyond working in a salon.
Content:
Beauty careers include hairstylist, makeup artist, esthetician, nail technician, and beauty therapist. Educational requirements vary from short courses to formal certifications. Career progression can be from assistant to manager or business owner. Needed skills include creativity, customer service, and technical knowledge. For example, a makeup artist might start assisting a professional then build their own client base. Some beauty professionals also work in fashion, film, or teach others their skills.
Class activity:
Students will research one beauty career of their choice and present the educational requirements and possible career path to the class.
Evaluation questions:
Name five beauty careers. What educational requirements are needed for a hairstylist? How can a beauty professional progress in their career? What skills are important for success in beauty careers? Where might a makeup artist work besides a salon?
Summary:
The beauty industry offers diverse career opportunities for those with the right skills and passion.

topics.title: Project Work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to collaborate in groups, design a beauty business plan, create product prototypes, and present their project to the class.
Introduction:
This week we will work on a group project to apply what we've learned about beauty businesses throughout the term.
Content:
The project involves creating a beauty business plan and product prototype. Groups of 4-5 students will choose either a salon concept or beauty product line. The business plan should include market analysis, services/products offered, pricing, and marketing strategy. The prototype could be a sample package design, service menu, or product sample. For example, a group might design a natural hair salon with locally-sourced products and traditional styling techniques. Each group will present their project at the end of the week.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups throughout the week to complete their beauty business project, with teacher guidance and feedback.
Evaluation questions:
What is included in a beauty business plan? Why is prototyping important? How should groups divide tasks effectively? What makes a good business presentation? How does this project relate to real beauty businesses?
Summary:
This project helps you apply theoretical knowledge to practical beauty business scenarios.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall and explain key concepts from the term, identify important topics for examination, and prepare study questions.
Introduction:
Next week we have our final examination. Today we will begin revising all the topics we covered this term to prepare.
Content:
We will review entrepreneurship, product knowledge, branding, marketing, business setup, health and safety, and career opportunities. Focus on definitions, procedures, and practical applications. Create study notes for each topic with examples. Pay special attention to steps in processes and safety procedures. For example, when revising health and safety, remember the first aid steps and sterilization methods. Group study can help reinforce learning through discussion.
Class activity:
Students will create flashcards for key terms and concepts, then quiz each other in small groups.
Evaluation questions:
What are the main topics we covered this term? What is the most important thing to remember about product safety? How do you calculate startup costs? What are the steps to create a brand? Why is health and safety important in salons?
Summary:
Effective revision helps ensure you are well-prepared for your final examination.

topics.title: Revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate understanding of all term concepts through practice questions and discussions, identify areas needing further study, and formulate examination strategies.
Introduction:
Continuing our preparation for final examination, today we will focus on practice questions and clarifying any remaining doubts.
Content:
We will go through practice examination questions covering all topics. Pay attention to how questions are worded and what information is required. Discuss different approaches to answering questions. Identify any topics that need more review and focus on those. Time management during examination is important - practice answering questions within time limits. Remember to read instructions carefully before starting your examination.
Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to answer practice examination questions, then discuss their answers with the class.
Evaluation questions:
How should you approach a multi-part question? What topics do you find most challenging? How can you manage your time during an examination? What should you do if you don't know an answer? Why is reading instructions important?
Summary:
Final revision helps build confidence and ensure you are ready for your examination.

topics.title: Examination / Closing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate knowledge and understanding of beauty and cosmetology concepts through final examination.
Introduction:
Today we will have our final examination to assess your understanding of the entire term's work in beauty and cosmetology.
Content:
The examination will cover all topics from this term including entrepreneurship, product knowledge, branding, marketing, business setup, health and safety, and career opportunities. Questions will include multiple choice, short answer, and practical application. You will have 90 minutes to complete the examination. Read all questions carefully before answering. Manage your time well and attempt all questions.
Class activity:
Students will individually complete the final examination paper.
Evaluation questions:
The final examination will serve as the evaluation for this week.
Summary:
This examination concludes your beauty and cosmetology studies for this term. Well done on your hard work throughout the term.
